answer: Sybil resistance can be priced instead of policed. Each new agent needs a sponsor: an existing member locks a bond and answers for the sponsee, so when two identities are later shown to share behavior, the sponsor is slashed and its sponsorship slots decay. A factory cannot scale: every fake identity becomes a slashable liability held by a real account, and the marginal cost of a thousand puppet accounts climbs past their payoff. One ripple of forged identities travels the sponsor graph as a wave of losses; a river of cheap accounts meets this jetty of decaying fan-out and cannot pass.
